messages:
alex: :rotating_light: Seeing a sustained latency burn for /v1/generate. Alerts triggered at 11:42UTC. p95 token latency jumped from ~28ms to ~140ms across a subset of routes. anyone on?
priya: on it. grabbing dashboards now. which customers/routes?
alex: mostly customer-route=chat-default and a couple of long-context workloads. Datapoints look like token-level latency spikes rather than client-side backlog.
marco: could be KV cache churn or a kernel fallback. earlier today we pushed a kernel selector tweak that increases preference for the AVX2 int8 path on longer sequences.
sasha: I see an adjacent deploy at 11:40 by eng-runtime (kernel-selector v2.7) — might be correlated. tagging release id 5f9c.
devon: pulling traces and flamegraphs. running quick profiler: ```
# sampled kernel latency (ms)
kernel_avx2_fp16: avg 12.3 p95 45.1
kernel_avx2_int8: avg 18.7 p95 120.4
kernel_gpu_opt: avg 9.1 p95 35.6
kv_lookup (host): avg 2.4 p95 40.2
enqueue_wait: avg 0.8 p95 3.2
```
marco: that kv_lookup p95 at 40ms is suspicious — looks like misses or a blocking lock. kv_cache.hit_ratio dropped from 0.97 to 0.62 around 11:38.
alex: I can repro locally with a synthetic workload that pins sequence length to 8k. KV cache eviction rate spikes with the new kernel selection because kernel variants change cache key prefixes.
priya: ok root cause hypothesis: kernel selector changed model_variant tags -> cache key namespace mismatch -> cache misses -> expensive KV reads to backing store -> per-token latency spike.
sasha: we should rollback kernel-selector change on prod if evidence solid. but quick mitigation: increase KV cache TTL and enable warm-cache prefetch for the impacted routes.
devon: opened a temporary dashboard panel showing token-level breakdown: `redwood.runtime.token_latency.{enqueue,kv_lookup,kernel_exec,network}`. current graph shows kv_lookup dominating p95. query: ```
avg:percentile(redwood.runtime.token_latency.kv_lookup{route:chat-default},95)
```
alex: suggested alert tweak: current latency burn alert triggers after 5m at 200% of SLO. Let's add a burn-rate alert that trips at 1.5x for 3m as warning, and paging threshold at 2x sustained for 6m.
priya: +1. I'll create a Datadog monitor for burn-rate with composite checks: token_p95 AND kv_lookup_p95. Also add anomaly detection on kv_cache.hit_ratio.
marco: to prevent recurrence we should make kernel selection not change external cache keys. I've queued a patch to seal the namespace mapping and to add a migration that backfills variant aliases.
sasha: deployment plan: 1) revert kernel-selector change -> hotfix 2) bump kv cache TTL for chat-default by 30s 3) enable prefetch for active sessions 4) roll forward kernel fix with aliasing. can we do revert now?
alex: revert approved. I'll ship the revert (release id 5f9d) and warm the cache via the batch prefetch job.
priya: pagerduty-bot: if pagerduty escalation is needed, what thresholds?
pagerduty-bot: configured escalation policy: page after 6m critical OR manual ack by oncall. current critical threshold will not page until 6m.
priya: change requested: page if token_p95 > 200ms AND kv_lookup_p95 > 80ms for 4m. leave warning for 2m at 150ms.
devon: updated dashboard: added per-route KPIs (token_p50/p95/p99, kv_hit_ratio, batching.avg_size, kernel_variant_counts). link: internal/grafana/d/rt-token-breakdown (will add panels for enqueue/kv/kernel).
marco: added a profiler job that will sample one request per 100ms for impacted route and upload trace id to Slack thread. sample output: ```
TRACE: e2b3-... duration=152ms
steps: enqueue=1.1ms, kv_lookup=67.8ms, kernel_exec=70.2ms, network=12.9ms
```
alex: after revert and prefetch we saw p95 drop to ~34ms within two minutes. KV hit ratio back to 0.95.
priya: awesome. action items: * Devs: root-cause patch for kernel selector aliasing (marco) * Infra: update alerting policy + burn rate thresholds (priya) * Observability: add token-level panel + composite monitor (devon) * Ops: run warm-prefetch job for top 10 routes (alex)
sasha: I'll schedule a quick postmortem doc and add timeline to incidents/ for RL meeting.
marco: will open PR with tests for namespace invariants and add a regression test that simulates variant tag drift.
priya: leaving one request: can we add a per-route safety net that disables variant switching if kv_hit_ratio drops > 10% within 2m? might prevent risky rollouts.
alex: good idea. adding feature flag to kernel-selector.
devon: I'll set up the anomaly detect monitor and run a replay on last 7 days to see false positive rate.
priya: thanks all. mark resolved for now — reopening if alerts reoccur. :thumbsup:
